title: Variant-specific KV residency & memory-profile tuning for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Create tuned memory profiles and KV-residency heuristics per model family (Llama 2 variants, Mistral 7B/15B, Qwen series) targeting 8k-64k long-context configs. These profiles should reduce GPU OOMs and fragmentation, increase effective batch concurrency for continuous batching, and improve tail latency under sustained traffic. Scope includes: 1) measurement harness for model-specific memory allocations during serving (tokens, KV growth, tensor lifetimes), 2) offline-fitting step to generate compact 'residency curves' that map sequence length distributions to preferred KV residency/eviction thresholds and allocation slabs, 3) runtime knobs to apply profiles and to switch gracefully between variants and quantization levels, 4) integration tests and perf dashboards to validate improvements across Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Automated profile generator produces a candidate profile for each model variant in the catalog (llama-2-13b, llama-2-70b, mistral-7b-instruct, mistral-15b, qwen-7b, qwen-14b) for long-context targets: 8k, 32k, 64k.
Per-model profile reduces OOM incidents by >= 90% on synthetic long-context replay compared to baseline generic profile at same batch/throughput settings.
Effective GPU batch concurrency improves by >= 20% (measured tokens/s per GPU) for at least 3 model variants under continuous batching workload.
No regression in median latency (>5%) for typical short-context requests (<=512 tokens).
Runtime feature flags exist to enable/disable per-model profiles and to fall back to generic profile on memory pressure events.
Profile artifacts stored in /models/profiles and surfaced in model catalog UI with versioning metadata.
technical_notes: KV residency: represent as percent residency per KV slab tier (e.g., full-kv, half-kv, ephemeral) and an eviction priority curve derived from token-pos distributions.
Memory measurements collected using instrumented allocator hooks + CUDA NVTX spans; capture peak device memory, fragmentation estimate (free list entropy), and active allocation lifetimes.
Offline fitting: run batch of calibration sequences sampled from customer probe sets and open evaluation prompts; fit piecewise-linear curves mapping seq_len->preferred_kv_limit.
Kernel/quantization considerations: 8-bit quantized kernels have different activation footprints; profiles must include quantization tag and an empirical inflation factor for activation buffers.
Compatibility: profiles must be compatible with continuous-batching runtime (preserve prefix KV reuse) and with multi-model co-location on Dedicated nodes.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Build measurement harness (allocator hooks, NVTX tagging, per-request allocation traces).
Week 2: Run calibration jobs across model variants and quant levels; collect dataset of allocation traces for 8k/32k/64k sequences.
Week 3: Implement offline fitter to generate residency curves + slab thresholds; create serialization format (profile v1 JSON with tags).
Week 4: Add runtime application logic to runtime scheduler (policy engine) to consult profile during request placement and KV evictions.
Week 5: End-to-end tests, perf runs, and dashboard plumbing; iterate on profile heuristics based on empirical results.
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator hooks and profile serialization/deserialization.
Integration test: replay recorded traces against runtime with and without per-model profile; assert OOM drop and latency targets.
Stress test: continuous-batching synthetic traffic generator that simulates mixed seq-lengths and co-located models for 6 hours.
A/B rollout in staging Dedicated pool with metrics collection (OOMs, tokens/s, p50/p95 latency) comparing generic vs per-model profiles.
Canary in production low-traffic region with automatic rollback if OOMs or error rate increase beyond threshold.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout tied to model catalog entry. Default: disabled for all models.
Enable for non-critical test customers and internal benchmarks for 48h; monitor telemetry.
Progressively enable for >5% Dedicated capacity where models are present, then 25%, then full, with 24h observation windows.
Fallback: runtime detects sustained memory pressure and switches to generic profile + alert to on-call.
tradeoffs: Overfitting risk: profiles derived from limited calibration sets may mispredict for diverse customer prompts; mitigate via runtime pressure detection and fallback.
Complexity: per-model profiles increase scheduler complexity and state; requires clear serialization and UX in model catalog to reduce support burden.
Storage: profile artifacts add small metadata per model (few KBs) but must be versioned for rollback and compatibility.
metrics: OOM incidents per 10k requests by model variant (target: -90%).
Tokens/second per GPU under continuous-batching (target: +20% for 3+ variants).
Median and P95 latency changes for short-context requests (target: <=5% median regression, p95 monitored).
Fragmentation estimate (bytes wasted per GPU) reduced vs baseline.
